appraisal_events.evidence: tel Aimé... s'en allait chercher nos rince-bouches avec le même sourire orgueilleusement modeste et savamment discret... Elle n'était pas de la race agréable et pleine de bonhomie dont Aimé faisait partie.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator warmly compares Aimé to a delighted hairdresser and a proud father, praising his tact and genuine good nature, and explicitly places him among 'la race agréable et pleine de bonhomie' in contrast to Françoise's pride.

appraisal_events.evidence: Françoise l'excusa d'être marquise... elle la préféra à toutes les personnes que nous connaissions. C'est qu'aussi aucune ne s'efforçait d'être aussi continuellement aimable.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator credits Mme de Villeparisis's unmatched, continual kindness (gifts, attentiveness) as winning over even the proud Françoise, presenting her amiability as a genuine, distinguishing virtue.

appraisal_events.evidence: la marquise prit l'habitude de venir tous les jours... s'asseoir un moment près de nous dans la salle à manger... Chaque fois que ma grand'mère remarquait un livre... une heure après un valet de chambre montait nous remettre livre ou fruits.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Villeparisis's daily visits and thoughtful gifts draw la grand-mère into a genuine, valued friendship with a marquise, marking her inclusion in esteemed company.

status_effects.explanation: Aimé is favorably characterized by the narrator as tactful and good-natured, elevated in contrast to Françoise's pride.
Her continual amiability and generosity toward the family, endorsed by the narrator, mark a positive local characterization.
She is drawn into a genuine daily friendship and receives gifts from Mme de Villeparisis, marking her inclusion in valued aristocratic company.

ambiguities: Mme de Villeparisis also shows mild tactlessness (questioning why grand-mère's daughter writes daily, calling Mme de Sévigné 'not natural'), and the narrator hedges that grand-mère's silence 'on peut croire' reflected disdain; this possible undercurrent of friction was left unscored since the hedge ('on peut croire') signals narrator uncertainty rather than a settled local event.

The opening line ('Ma vie dans l'hôtel était rendue... triste parce que je n'y avais pas de relations') could suggest le narrateur is excluded from valued company, but it reads as retrospective/essayistic scene-setting rather than a staged social interaction, so le narrateur was not scored per the candidate rules.
